Overview

The Sprott Physical Silver Trust (PSLV) is a closed-end trust that invests in unencumbered and fully-allocated London Good Delivery (“LGD”) silver bars.

Our goal is to provide a secure, convenient and exchange-traded investment alternative for investors who want to hold physical silver.

Investing in PSLV offers several compelling reasons: you benefit from fully allocated silver bullion, it’s redeemable for metals, secure storage you can trust, potential tax advantages, ease of purchase, sale, and ownership, and the liquidity of your investment.

Please note, all Sprott Physical Trusts are considered PFICs, please review the Tax Guide.

Tax & Resources

Tax Treatment for U.S. Investors

Please Note: The tax information provided by Sprott is for general informational purposes only and should not be considered tax, legal or accounting advice. Because each investor’s situation is unique, you should consult your own tax advisor or legal professional before making any investment decisions.

For U.S. investors, Sprott Physical Bullion Trusts may offer more favorable tax treatment* than owning metals directly or through certain ETFs. However, because the Trusts would generally be classified as Passive Foreign Investment Companies (PFICs) by the IRS, U.S. investors generally must make a timely Qualified Electing Fund (QEF) election by filing IRS Form 8621 in the first taxable year they own Trust units to preserve capital gains tax treatment (generally applicable to taxable accounts, not qualified retirement accounts, such as IRAs). Once the QEF election is made, Form 8621 must be filed annually for as long as the Trust units are held, even in years with no distributions from the Trust. 

*Resources: Visit Tax Guide for Additional Information 

What is a PFIC?

“PFIC” stands for “Passive Foreign Investment Company.” A foreign corporation such as the Sprott Physical Bullion Trusts (“the Trusts”) will be treated as a PFIC for any taxable year if either of the following is true: (a) more than 75% of its gross income is from passive sources or (b) at least 50% of its assets are held for the production of passive income.

Commentary

Gold and Silver Weather a Perfect Storm as Demand Holds Firm

BY PAUL WONG AND KENNY ZHU  · 11/13/2026
Gold came under significant pressure in October, falling 6.80% to $3,874.62 per ounce and closing the month at a 52-week low. The weakness occurred despite a 35-basis-point decline in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield to 4.93%, even as the U.S. dollar strengthened modestly and remained near its 52-week highs. Precious metals broadly underperformed, with silver declining 18.74% and gold miner stocks falling 11.90% over the month, although miner stocks remained above their summer lows.

Asset TV Masterclass: Commodities & Energy

BY ED COYNE · 10/29/2026
Explore the forces reshaping commodities and natural resource investing, from rising demand for critical minerals to renewed interest in nuclear energy. Ed Coyne and Douglas Daly discuss supply constraints, geopolitics, electrification and the investment outlook for copper, uranium, silver, gold and rare earths. They also examine how natural resources may provide diversification and inflation sensitivity within a broader portfolio.

The Miners Take the Lead: What's Driving Gold & Silver Equities

SPROTT WEBCAST REPLAY · 10/25/2026
Gold and silver mining equities have outperformed the underlying metals year-to-date, supported by improving margins, stronger free cash flow potential and renewed investor interest in the operational leverage miners can offer. Watch the webcast replay to learn why Sprott Portfolio Managers Maria Smirnova and Justin Tolman believe mining equities may have entered a new phase of leadership, and what that could mean for precious metals allocations.

Silver’s Next Rally and Why Miners Could Outperform

BY KENNY ZHU · 10/20/2026
Proactive's Stephen Gunnion interviews Kenny Zhu on the forces shaping silver’s volatile price action, including monetary conditions, industrial demand and a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit. Zhu explains why growing demand from electronics, AI infrastructure and China’s manufacturing sector could continue to support the market. He outlines why Sprott favors silver miners, particularly primary producers, for their operating leverage, margin potential and comparatively attractive valuations.

Gold Holds Its Ground as Real Yields Surge

BY PAUL WONG AND KENNY ZHU · 10/8/2026
Gold held firm in September as real yields surged, suggesting investors are increasingly focused on fiscal strain and reserve diversification. We examine why rising Treasury yields can deepen the fiscal challenge and why gold’s role outside the sovereign liability structure matters. We also assess silver’s rate headwinds, resilient Chinese demand and industrial support.

Gold and Silver Surge as Fiscal Credibility Erodes

BY PAUL WONG AND KENNY ZHU · 9/8/2026
Gold and silver surged in August as rising debt, higher term premiums and growing concerns about U.S. fiscal credibility revived the currency debasement trade. Gold is increasingly behaving as “outside money,” supported by strong central bank buying, while silver is benefiting from renewed investor demand, persistent supply deficits and tight inventories. We examine why these forces may be setting the stage for the next move in precious metals.

How to Obtain Physical Certificates

In the United States, shareholders can contact the Computershare call center at 800.446.2617 or go to computershare.com and access a transfer form by creating an account.

In Canada, shareholders can direct their broker to withdraw units from CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. When the broker puts in the withdrawal, the transfer agent in Canada, TSX Trust Company, will issue physical certificates to the broker.

How to Hold Units in Your Name

Once you have purchased Trust units through a third-party financial professional, the Direct Registration System (DRS) option gives you the ability to transfer the units you own from your broker to the Trust's transfer agents (Computershare for U.S. unitholders and TSX Trust Company for Canadian unitholders). DRS is the electronic or book-entry form of security ownership offered by and only through transfer agents and allows a unitholder to hold Trust units in that holder’s name directly as opposed to electronic security ownership through a broker. The DRS option went into effect on October 5, 2017, for unitholders of each of the Trusts (read press release).

How to Redeem for Physical Bullion

Sprott Physical Bullion Trust unitholders have the right to redeem for physical metals on a monthly basis, subject to meeting the minimum redemption amount. To submit a request for physical redemption, a unitholder must complete the required redemption form for the specific Trust from which they wish to redeem units.

The Intraday Indicative Value is a real-time estimate of one unit of the Trust, based on the most recent prices of its underlying securities. This value is refreshed approximately every 15 seconds and serves as a time-specific gauge of the Trust's current market price.                         
Intraday Premium/Discount Calculation is the premium/discount expressed as a percentage of the trust unit's Last Traded Price against the Intraday Indicative Value. Intraday data only populates during active market trading hours.                         
In US Dollars. Data Last updated Thursday, November 19, 2026 6:00 PM EST. The amount the Trust's closing price is trading above or below the reported NAV (net asset value), expressed as a percentage of the NAV. When the Trust's closing price is greater than the Trust's NAV, it is trading at a “premium” and the percentage is expressed as a positive number. When the Trust's closing price is less than the Trust's NAV, it is trading at a “discount” and the percentage is expressed as a negative number.

The Trust’s assets include fully allocated , unencumbered physical bullion and a small percentage of cash. The amount of physical bullion and the net cash amount (cash less liabilities) calculated for a given number of Units is based on the latest net asset value for the Trust. The Units trade on the TSX and NYSE ARCA and the market price for the units will typically vary from the net asset value of the units.
